long_biography.plain_text:
Sent to study in Tampa, Florida, Al Moosa returned to Dubai in 1974 amid rapid infrastructure growth. He described spotting an opening in dredging and arranged an introduction between a foreign contractor and the ruler's advisers. The resulting participation in Dubai Creek work became an early commercial foothold. The following year he established the enterprise that bears his name, then expanded across contracting, transport, manufacturing and trading.

His most visible later undertaking was Falconcity of Wonders, launched in 2005 on more than 41 million square feet. The falcon-shaped plan combined residences with offices, retail, tourism and hospitality, using architectural landmarks as organizing themes. As chairman and chief executive, Al Moosa framed it as a self-contained city and an investment destination. The venture remains his enterprise's largest, with residential areas and planned commercial, retail, tourism and hospitality districts organized around the falcon motif.
